_note: The film room (docs/FILM.md): public Pokémon Showdown replays read turn by turn. Every switch and move is a row with the game state when it happened; every Pokémon keeps the order it came in, the order it used its moves, and every part of its build the battle revealed. Nothing here is canon: a study becomes a card in the intake inbox, and only approved claims land.

sources._note: Showdown's public replay server. Search returns up to 51 replays a page, newest first; 'before' (an upload time) pages back. Smogon tournament games come back in the same search with ids starting 'smogtours-': no ladder rating, but the highest level of play. Replays are public records; chat lines are never stored.

store._note: Fetched replays are cached exactly as Showdown sent them (data/ is rebuilt by fetching and never committed). A study is saved beside them for the page and the cards.

formats._note: The formats the room reads, the generation each is, and the game the role engine reads its sets in (the era: moves, types, abilities).

state._note: The game state from the side about to act, before it acts. Ahead or behind on Pokémon left first; when the count is level, the side up by at least hp_margin of a Pokémon's HP (summed across the team, unseen members counted healthy) is ahead.

order._note: How the room reads order. The lead comes in before turn 1. A member 'held back' is one first seen after this share of the battle had passed. The closer lands the battle's last knockout.

actions._note: What each chosen action counts as, for the action mix by game state. A move is read through the role engine's move categories (trainers/roles.json); the first group it matches names it. Aggression uses the playsheet's own finisher and attrition lists (trainers/config.json playsheet.aggression), so a measured ratio and a moveset's ratio mean the same thing.

study._note: What a study keeps. A revealed set is the moves, item and ability one Pokémon showed in one battle; it's read only when it showed at least min_moves_to_read moves (fewer reads as noise). A species' variants are its revealed sets clustered by what they share: a set joins the variant whose consensus moves (and item) it overlaps most, if the overlap (shared / the smaller of the two) is at least variant_overlap; otherwise it starts a new one. Fuller sets are placed first. Each variant is then read through the role engine. A team's shape counts only teams with at most shape_max_unread members too little seen. Top plays count once per battle, so one long game can't swamp them. Cores are two Pokémon on the same team.

cards._note: What a study proposes to canon. Observations are tallies (sample_size is how many battles or times it was seen), each citing up to examples_per_claim of the battles it happened in; per_kind caps how many of each kind a card carries. Builds are variants seen in enough battles. A player mapped to a trainer id here files under that trainer (your own Showdown name to 'me'); anyone else as 'showdown:<name>', a field study as 'field:<format>'.

usage._note: Smogon's monthly usage statistics (film/usage.py): smogon.com/stats, the 'chaos' JSON per format and rating cutoff. Public statistics about real play, cited per use. The cutoff is the rating floor of the battles counted (0, 1500, 1630 or 1760). Shares under floor % are left out; checks need more than checks_min_n matchups, Smogon's own cutoff (its moveset files list a check only past 20), and rank on the unrounded score.
usage._aliases_note: Gen 2 item ids that PokeAPI lists under their modern names or not at all (E-023), as the Gen 2 games spell them.

book._note: The builds book (film/buildbook.py): the top species by usage, up to sets_per_species replay variants each (a variant past the first needs min_battles), plus the ladder's most-used moves when no variant already has them; the month's top team styles and leads.
book._fit_note: A set's spread is fitted to the roles that define it: its primary and secondary, leaving out fit_skip_roles (setting sand reads the same whatever the spread, so a Tyranitar's spread follows what it does besides).
